groups.summary: The entry points of the heliaPROFILER Python API: one call, one session, and the progress stream they report through.
The run description: what to profile, on what, how, and what to write out. Every field of a YAML config file lands in one of these.
Replayable run plans: every resolved setting, the model's hash and the toolchain and runtime identities, saved so another host can rebuild the same run.

Build once, run later: a frozen plan's compiled firmware, bound to its plan and saved so any host can verify, relocate and capture from it, each run saved as a verifiable result that loads back on any host, how model state carries across a run's invocations, and the build and capture records a compiled build and a run result carry. The hpx freeze, hpx build, hpx validate build and hpx run commands drive the same flow from the command line.

What a run is built for and captured under: the typed fixture that pins a model's input bytes and declares its outputs, the tensors' element types and quantization, how the run is timed, the prepared runtime a build links, the board guard a capture answers to, the model analysis that lists a model's inputs and outputs, and the targets and IO types this heliaPROFILER builds.

Who vouches for the board a run flashes and the instrument it powers or measures with: the guard protocols a capture consults, the operator guard the command line uses, and the rail and supply requests a power run selects.
What a run captures from the board: the capture result, its timing and memory, and the power and PSRAM observations a capture can carry.
The runtimes a build links and how they are identified: prepared upstream archives, their verified manifests, and the kernel, runtime and engine sources a build records.
The compiled firmware a build produces and what it recorded: the build record, its memory plan, toolchain and PSRAM weight placement.
What this HPX can run: engines, data types and qualified targets.

Shared identity vocabulary: the identity of a captured run and the build, run, energy, runtime and kernel facts it names, canonical engine and kernel names with today's spellings as aliases, unknown facts that carry their reason, and the semantic hashes that name their kind and basis version.
Power capture settings: which instrument measures the rail, how it is wired to the board, and which window of the run is integrated.
The fixed vocabularies a configuration selects from: engines, toolchains, capture transports, memory placements and reset strategies.
What this build of heliaPROFILER is qualified against: the board, engine and toolchain matrix, and the locked dependency revisions a run was produced with.
The runtime versions this heliaPROFILER records, and whether each is qualified for a precision on a board and clock.
What a profiling run produces: the run result, its per-layer and PMU detail, and the firmware and run metadata that say how it was measured.
The on-disk index of a run directory: the artifacts it holds, the issues raised against it, and whether its numbers may be used.
What a power capture produces: the measured result, the observations behind it, and the on-device summary the firmware reports.
The provenance of a power number: how it was observed, what the measurement boundary included, and whether the capture holds together.
Comparing two runs and judging one: the comparability rules that decide whether a comparison is meaningful, and the metric policies that turn numbers into a verdict.
Checking a run's outputs: reference outputs from host LiteRT or caller files, compared tensor by tensor, with a verdict only when a tolerance is given.
The static cost model of a network, read from the model file before anything is built or run.
Collecting a redacted support bundle from a run directory, and reading one back.
The exception hierarchy every heliaPROFILER failure is raised through, rooted at HpxError.
Packaged model and config assets used by the examples, smoke tests and tutorials.
